wv_malone_boulder.blurb: A low, partly tucked-away sandstone boulder in the Cotton Bottom bouldering zone of the lower New River Gorge, sitting just upstream of the Slitty Titty boulder. Ten problems, all bouldering, run from the easiest grades up to V8, with the bulk clustered around V4. The left side holds a well-known lowball sloper traverse that suits a few pads, while the right side tucks into a cave-like hollow with harder lines. Expect slopers, heel hooks and toe hooks over technical power. The boulder is short, so landings are mostly a matter of good pad placement. It makes a sensible stop when you are working the whole Cotton Bottom group.

wv_slitty_titty_boulder.blurb: A roadside sandstone boulder in the Cotton Bottom zone of the lower New River Gorge, a short downhill stroll from the pull-off and a little left of where you arrive. It carries ten bouldering problems, mostly easy to middle grades: a few V0 to V2 warm-ups, a block of V4 lines, and one V5 at the top end. The style is technical, vertical climbing on small holds, and its namesake traverse has a reputation for feeling harder than the number. That mix of moderates makes it a good first stop for a session, and the whole zone is a handy fallback when other gorge boulders are not in shape.

wv_rusty_red_boulder.blurb: A small sandstone boulder in the Lower Rock City part of Coopers Rock State Forest in northern West Virginia, found by walking on beyond the Jekyll and Hyde block. Its best feature is a striking rust-coloured face on the uphill side that holds several problems. Ten boulder problems in all, roughly ten feet tall: mostly V0 to V2 slabs, arete and mantle lines, with a couple of V5 problems for stronger climbers. A friendly pick for easier grades, and a quick add-on if you are already circulating through Lower Rock City. Brush off holds after use and avoid climbing it when the rock is damp.

wv_second_wall.blurb: A short sandstone cliff band at Coopers Rock State Forest in northern West Virginia, forming part of the busy Tilted Tree zone and running along the same line of rock as First Wall. Ten boulder problems cover a wide range, from an easy V0 and V1 through a cluster of V4 lines to a couple of hard V7 problems, so it suits both a casual session and a project day. The cliff is low and clean enough to boulder comfortably. Tilted Tree gets crowded on weekends, so a weekday visit is quieter. Bring a couple of pads.
